villain.simpleMeaning: A bad character in a story who often works against the hero.
villain.example: A villain can be unpleasant and still make a story difficult to leave.

threat.simpleMeaning: Something that may cause harm or danger.
threat.example: Darth Vader brings threat, but his past also creates a question about change.

morbid curiosity.simpleMeaning: The wish to learn about dark, dangerous, or frightening subjects.
morbid curiosity.example: Psychologist Coltan Scrivner developed a 24-question Morbid Curiosity Scale.

motive.simpleMeaning: A reason why someone does something.
motive.example: We want to know the motive, plan, or hidden history.

moral ambiguity.simpleMeaning: A situation where right and wrong are not completely clear.
moral ambiguity.example: This creates moral ambiguity: we can understand part of the character without approving of the action.

suspense.simpleMeaning: The nervous feeling of not knowing what will happen next.
suspense.translationJa: 何が起こるか分からない緊張感

benign masochism.simpleMeaning: Enjoying an unpleasant feeling when you know it is safe.
benign masochism.translationJa: 安全だと分かっている不快感を楽しむこと
benign masochism.example: The researchers called this benign masochism.

close.simpleMeaning: To shut something so it is no longer open.
close.example: Your body reacts, but your mind knows you can pause the film or close the book.

darth vader.simpleMeaning: The masked villain in Star Wars, once a Jedi named Anakin Skywalker.
darth vader.example: Darth Vader brings threat, but his past also creates a question about change.

iago.simpleMeaning: The villain in Shakespeare's Othello who secretly traps other characters.
iago.example: Iago in Othello tells the audience about his plan, so suspense comes from waiting to see who will understand the trap.

frankenstein's creature.simpleMeaning: The being made in Mary Shelley's novel; he causes harm but also feels rejected and alone.
frankenstein's creature.translationJa: フランケンシュタインの怪物
frankenstein's creature.example: Frankenstein's creature causes harm but also describes rejection and loneliness, which creates moral ambiguity.
